A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KVLink. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the figures, tables, and equations support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA, summarization, general-capability, and latency experiments, plus data-mixture and answer-position analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for an 8B model and compressed-cache comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 Section 2.4 and Appendix A.6 introduce compressed-cache linking, including a modified ANLLM compressor with fixed-length chunks, multiple anchor tokens, altered attention masks, and compression pretraining followed by QA tuning. The original positional re-encoding, link-token mechanism, and mixed-data training remain; the latter is relocated to the appendix.

E1.justification: The reported training sources and QA, summarization, and general-capability benchmarks remain unchanged. The training-mixture table is retained as v2 Table 4. The added 8B and compression experiments use the existing data and tasks under additional model and processing configurations.

E2.justification: PromptCache, CacheBlend, BlockAttention, and the full-encoding reference models remain in the original comparisons. New Table 3 compares LLMLingua prompt compression, citing LLMLingua-2, against the modified ANLLM compressor, each evaluated with BlockAttention and KVLink.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.1-8B evaluations and a compressed-cache protocol using the 1B model, 50% and 75% compression, and QA tuning on 2WikiMQA and TriviaQA. The retained experiments keep their retrieval procedures, metrics, and stated 6,000-step, batch-size-64 training configuration.

E4.justification: v2 Section 3.5 and Table 3 add an analysis of accuracy under two compression rates and two compression approaches, testing whether link tokens mitigate compression losses. The existing data-mixture ablations and answer-document-position analysis in Appendices A.4-A.5 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average TTFT over 100 runs following 10 warm-up trials. v2 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; its additional accuracy tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The 1B and 3B entries in Tables 1-2 and the data-mixture ablation values are unchanged. v2 adds 8B results and the compression results in Table 3. Timing values are replaced: at 5,000 tokens, standard-decoding TTFT changes from 0.267 to 0.885 seconds, while both KVLink variants change from 0.029 to 0.032 seconds. The PDFs do not establish matching timing hardware and backbones, so this is not an established same-setting speed improvement.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.4 adds a mathematical definition of fixed-size chunks for anchor compression. Its equation indexes chunks through N although the preceding text specifies N/s chunks. The existing RoPE and link-token mathematics remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central cache-reuse and approximately 4% QA-improvement claims remain. v2 promotes compression compatibility into the abstract and introduction, raises the maximum TTFT-reduction claim from 90% to 96%, and stops presenting mixed-data fine-tuning as a separate key contribution while retaining that training procedure.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning out-of-domain generalization and information retention under compression. Its limitations now discuss residual compression losses and difficulties storing variable-length caches, replacing v1's explicit warning about fine-tuning costs for large models and refining the existing storage limitation.

D1.justification: v2 documents 100-token compression chunks and first-half compression with prediction loss on the second half, followed by QA tuning. Reported training hardware changes from eight A100 GPUs to eight H100 GPUs. The abstract replaces the public repository link with a statement that code is in supplementary material; actual supplementary-code availability cannot be verified from these PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds LLMLingua-2 and Anchor-based Large Language Models, explaining its modifications to the latter. Section 4 also adds a RAG discussion covering works such as LongMem, Self-RAG, and RAFT. Positioning against the original cache-reuse baselines remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted edits revise the abstract and results discussion; mixed-data training, limitations, and societal impact move into the appendix, and the submission checklist is separated into licensing and LLM-usage sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. v1 Figures 2-3 become a combined v2 Figure 2; the latency chart is rescaled, Tables 1-2 gain 8B panels, and a compression table and training diagram are added. Existing appendix displays are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 partly addresses v1's acknowledged storage problem with an explicit compression method and evaluated accuracy tradeoffs, while the 8B results strengthen evidence across model sizes. These useful gains are limited by overgeneralized claims: Table 3 includes exceptions to consistent improvement, such as MuSiQue at 75% prompt compression scoring 6.5 for KVLink versus 7.1 for BlockAttention. The revised timing claims lack sufficient comparability details, and the code-access statement becomes less actionable.
